heroIntro: Commercial lending and corporate financing in Bangladesh are governed by one of the most stringent, creditor-friendly debtor statutes in emerging Asia: the **Money Loan Court Act, 2003 (অর্থ ঋণ আদালত আইন, ২০০৩ / Artha Rin Adalat Ain)**. For business owners, corporate managing directors, board shareholders, and Non-Resident Bangladeshi (NRB) personal guarantors, facing financial distress or loan default triggers draconian legal consequences. Commercial financial institutions (banks and NBFIs) are armed with sweeping statutory powers: summary extra-judicial auction of mortgaged assets under Section 12, pre-judgment asset attachments under Section 25, civil arrest warrants and imprisonment up to 6 months under Section 34, nationwide Credit Information Bureau (CIB) blacklisting, and freezing of all corporate and personal bank accounts. Navigating Artha Rin litigation requires strategic commercial defense: identifying fatal banking procedural defects, challenging inflated interest calculations under Bangladesh Bank master circulars, obtaining High Court stay orders against premature auctions, and negotiating loan rescheduling via down-payment restructuring.

quickAnswer.heading: Artha Rin Defense: 7 Core Tactical Rules
points: Specialized Jurisdiction: Money loan recovery cases are tried exclusively by the Money Loan Court (অর্থ ঋণ আদালত) established under the 2003 Act.
Mandatory Section 12 Auction Prerequisite: Under Section 12(1), a bank CANNOT institute an Artha Rin suit without first attempting to sell mortgaged immovable property through a public auction.
Contesting Inflated Statements: Financial institutions frequently compound illegal penal interest, unapproved service charges, or violate Bangladesh Bank single-digit interest caps.
Section 25 Pre-Judgment Attachment: Banks often pray for the attachment of unmortgaged personal assets of directors and guarantors; timely legal objections can defeat these motions.
Section 34 Civil Imprisonment: In execution proceedings, the judge can order civil imprisonment of the defaulter or guarantor for up to 6 months.
High Court Writ Remedies: When banks violate statutory auction procedures or arbitrary CIB reporting, the High Court Division under Article 102 can grant stay orders.
Rescheduling Protocols: Defaulters can leverage BRPD Master Circulars to reschedule non-performing loans (NPLs) with minimal down-payments (2% to 10%) over extended repayment tenures.

sections.h2: 1. The Statutory Architecture: Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 & Creditor Powers
sections.content:
Following the failure of the 1990 Money Loan Court Act to stem soaring non-performing loans (NPLs), the parliament enacted the Money Loan Court Act, 2003 (Act No. VIII of 2003) to create specialized, fast-track summary courts dedicated exclusively to financial debt recovery.

Key statutory features that every borrower must understand:

  • Exclusive Jurisdiction (Section 5): No regular civil court can entertain any suit or claim regarding financial loan recovery; jurisdiction lies exclusively with the Artha Rin Adalat.
  • Time-Bound Adjudication: The statute mandates that trial must be completed within 90 working days (extendable by 30 days) from the date of framing issues under Section 17.
  • Overriding Statutory Effect (Section 3): The provisions of the 2003 Act override any other conflicting general law, including the Code of Civil Procedure 1908 and Contract Act 1872.
  • Restriction on Injunctions: Civil courts are expressly barred from issuing temporary injunctions against Money Loan Court proceedings or bank auctions.

sections.h2: 2. The Mandatory Pre-Suit Prerequisite: Section 12 Public Auction Rules
sections.content:
The single most potent statutory defense available to a borrower in the preliminary phase of a loan dispute is Section 12 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003:

Section 12(1) Mandatory Condition Precedent: Where any financial loan is secured by a registered mortgage of immovable property or pledge of goods, the financial institution CANNOT institute any suit in the Money Loan Court without first attempting to sell the mortgaged property through a public auction in accordance with the provisions of Section 12.

Mandatory Bank Auction Requirements:

  • Publication of a formal public auction notice in at least one widely circulated national Bengali daily newspaper giving at least 15 days clear notice.
  • The auction notice must contain the exact property schedule, land area, Mouza, Khatian, and Dag numbers.
  • If the bank files a lawsuit without publishing a valid Section 12 auction notice, or if the notice was published in a clandestine, obscure local leaflet to conceal it from the borrower, the plaint is liable to immediate rejection under Order VII Rule 11 CPC for non-compliance with statutory conditions precedent.

sections.content:

sections.h2: 4. Drafting the Written Statement: Contesting Penal Interest & Ledger Fraud
sections.content:
When served with summons, the borrower must submit a comprehensive Written Statement (লিখিত জবাব) under Section 16 of the Act. Effective grounds of defense include:

  • Compounded Penal Interest Violations: Bangladesh Bank BRPD Circulars strictly prohibit banks from charging compounded interest or applying extortionate hidden service charges beyond statutory lending caps.
  • Discrepancies in Bank Ledgers: Forcing the bank to produce certified statements of accounts under the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891. In practice, bank account statements frequently conceal unauthorized debits and miscalculate interest during grace periods.
  • Challenging the Mortgage Valuation: Proving that the bank has deliberately under-valued the mortgaged assets to pave the way for a distress sale to syndicate insiders.
  • Disputing Personal Guarantee Signatures: If an expatriate director was abroad when loan renewal agreements or guarantees were executed, challenging forged signatures via CID forensic handwriting analysis.

Under Section 6(1) and 6(2) of the Act, a financial institution must sue both the principal borrower and all personal or third-party guarantors in the identical lawsuit:

The Guarantor's Safeguard (Section 6(5)): Under Section 6(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, the decree shall be executed first against the principal borrower and by selling the mortgaged property. The personal property of the third-party guarantor cannot be attached or sold until the primary mortgaged securities of the principal debtor are exhausted.

Expatriate family members who signed routine third-party personal guarantees can utilize Section 6(5) to insulate their personal properties from premature bank execution.

Under Section 25 of the 2003 Act, banks routinely file aggressive applications praying for the attachment before judgment (রায়পূর্ব ক্রোক) of unmortgaged personal properties, bank deposits, and factory assets belonging to company directors:

  • The bank must prove that the defendant is about to dispose of or remove property from the court's jurisdiction with intent to obstruct execution.
  • Our defense counsel files a counter-objection establishing that the existing mortgaged property has sufficient market valuation to satisfy the claim, rendering Section 25 attachments legally redundant and punitive.

sections.h2: 7. Execution Proceedings (অর্থ জারী মামলা) & Section 34 Civil Imprisonment
sections.content:
Once the Artha Rin Adalat passes a decree in favor of the bank, the bank institutes an Execution Case (অর্থ জারী মামলা) under Section 28 of the Act:

  1. Section 33 Public Auction: The court conducts judicial public auctions to sell the mortgaged property. If no bidder offers an adequate price, the court vests ownership in the bank under Section 33(5) with a certificate of possession.
  2. Section 34 Civil Imprisonment: If decretal dues remain unsatisfied, the court can issue a warrant of arrest committing the judgment-debtor or directors to civil imprisonment for up to six (6) months.
  3. Release from Imprisonment: Imprisonment does not extinguish the debt, but once the 6-month term expires, the debtor cannot be imprisoned again for the same decree.

sections.h2: 8. High Court Writ Petitions Against Arbitrary Bank Auctions & CIB Listing
sections.content:
Because Section 41 of the Act requires a borrower to deposit 50% of the decretal amount in cash to prefer an appeal, appealing within the statutory system is financially prohibitive. The premier constitutional defense is moving the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh under Article 102:

  • Writ Against Illegal Section 12 Auctions: If the bank published an auction notice violating the 15-day statutory rule or misrepresenting land acreage, the High Court issues an immediate Stay Order halting the auction.
  • Writ Against CIB Blacklisting: If a bank unlawfully reports a director or guarantor as a willful defaulter in violation of Bangladesh Bank restructuring guidelines, the High Court issues a Writ of Mandamus directing the Credit Information Bureau (CIB) to suspend the classification, enabling the company to open letters of credit (L/Cs) and conduct operations.

sections.h2: 9. Loan Rescheduling & One-Time Settlement (OTS) Under Bangladesh Bank Circulars
sections.content:
While courtroom litigation proceeds, the ultimate commercial solution is structuring a Loan Rescheduling or One-Time Settlement (OTS / এককালীন নিষ্পত্তি) under Bangladesh Bank Master Circulars (e.g. BRPD Circular No. 16/2019 and subsequent revisions):

  • Down-Payment Negotiation: Borrowers can apply to restructure loans upon depositing a nominal down-payment (typically 2% to 10% of total liability).
  • Interest Waiver (সুদ মওকুফ): Commercial banks have board authority to waive unapplied interest, penal interest, and compound interest, settling the debt strictly on the cost of funds or principal balance.
  • Exit Tenure: Repayment of the remaining balance is amortized over an extended horizon of 5 to 10 years, during which the Artha Rin lawsuit remains stayed.

sections.h2: 10. Real-Life Case Study: Halting BDT 18 Crore Commercial Factory Auction in Savar
sections.content:
Background: A ready-made garments (RMG) manufacturing export firm in Savar, co-owned by an expatriate director in Canada, faced an Artha Rin lawsuit for BDT 18.5 Crore filed by a commercial private bank. The bank hurriedly published an auction notice under Section 12 aiming to sell the factory and prime land worth BDT 35 Crore at a distress valuation of BDT 12 Crore.

Chamber Legal Rescue:

  1. Discovered that the bank failed to provide 15 days statutory notice and omitted the Mouza JL number from the newspaper advertisement.
  2. Filed an urgent Constitutional Writ Petition under Article 102 before the High Court Division.
  3. The High Court Division stayed the auction and issued a Rule Nisi directing Bangladesh Bank to audit the account's compound interest calculations.
  4. Armed with the High Court stay order, our team engaged the bank's Managing Director and Board of Directors in compromise negotiations under BRPD Master Circulars.
  5. The bank agreed to waive BDT 4.2 Crore in penal interest, accepted a 5% down-payment, and restructured the remaining BDT 14.3 Crore over an 8-year tenure. The factory continued unhindered export operations.

faqs.question: Can I be arrested or imprisoned for defaulting on a bank loan in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Under Section 34 of the Money Loan Court Act 2003, during execution proceedings (অর্থ জারী মামলা), the judge can order civil imprisonment of the judgment-debtor or corporate directors for up to six (6) months if the debt remains unpaid.

faqs.question: Can an NRB director or guarantor be stopped at Dhaka airport due to a bank loan?
faqs.answer: If the Money Loan Court or a criminal court has issued a civil warrant of arrest or travel restriction under Section 34, airport immigration will detain the traveler. However, an arbitrary travel ban without a court order can be quashed via High Court writ.

faqs.question: Can a bank sell my mortgaged property without going to court?
faqs.answer: Under Section 12 of the 2003 Act, a bank MUST attempt a public auction before filing a suit, but they cannot forcefully evict or seize physical possession without obtaining an execution decree from the Money Loan Court.

faqs.question: What is CIB blacklisting in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: The Credit Information Bureau (CIB) of Bangladesh Bank maintains credit history records. A defaulter classification bars the individual and associated corporate entities from borrowing, opening L/Cs, or acting as company directors.

faqs.question: How much down-payment is required to reschedule a bank loan in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Under Bangladesh Bank BRPD Master Circulars, down-payments typically range between 2% to 10% of the outstanding loan liability depending on the restructuring policy and bank board approval.

faqs.question: Can an Artha Rin lawsuit be settled out of court through Solenama?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under Section 22 and 24 of the Act, parties can settle amicably through alternative dispute resolution (ADR) or in-court compromise (আপসনামা), and the court will dispose of the suit based on the agreed terms.

faqs.question: What percentage of the decretal amount must be deposited to appeal an Artha Rin judgment?
faqs.answer: Under Section 41(2) of the Act, a judgment-debtor must deposit fifty percent (50%) of the decretal amount (or equivalent bank guarantee) to file an appeal before the High Court Division.

faqs.question: Can personal unmortgaged property be seized for a company bank loan?
faqs.answer: Only if the individual signed an express Personal Guarantee. Even then, under Section 6(5), the bank must exhaust the primary mortgaged company assets before attaching the guarantor's personal estate.
